newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks seen positive at open.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks seen positive at open.

text.p: * Toronto stocks were expected to rise slightly at the open after the Liberals maintained their electoral majority. * But traders said the market would likely follow New York's lead.

Toronto stocks were expected to open on a positive note on Tuesday as Prime Minister Jean Chretien's Liberals maintained their majority government and the separatist Bloc Quebecois slipped in popularity.
"I think initially the reaction probably will be positive because there have been times in the last couple of weeks that people thought there was going to be a minority government," one trader said.
But he said the status-quo result will likely leave the market looking to New York for overall direction.
"We have (U.S.) leading indicators at 10 o'clock (1400 GMT), which may cause the market to move around one way or the other," the trader said.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index closed 23.96 points higher on Monday at 6406.08.

Votes were tallied late on Monday following Canada's federal election. The Liberals were re-elected to a thin parliamentary majority of 155 seats, while the right-wing Reform party took 60 seats to form the official opposition as expected. The separatist Bloc Quebecois slipped in popularity, taking 44 seats, while the Conservatives and New Democrats gained ground, winning 20 and 21 seats, respectively.
* Inco Ltd's Sudbury workers walked off the job late on Monday after voting to reject the tentative agreement reached last week between the nickel giant and the United Steelworkers of America.
